# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, but I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I cannot reach Blind directly at all; Blind can only be reached by Deaf (through gesture, but Blind can't see gestures either!). Wait - let me reconsider the reach.

Actually, checking the channels: I gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb and see my gestures. Blind can hear speech and feel the bomb, but cannot see gestures. So I cannot reach Blind directly - I need Deaf to relay by speaking (since Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear).

The manual says: whatever light is lit, cut the corresponding wire color. I need to wait to learn what light is on the bomb from Deaf (via gesture back to me... but Deaf gestures only reach those who can see, and I cannot see). So Deaf must speak the light color, which only Blind and Mute... wait, I cannot hear either since I'm Mute but "cannot speak" - can I hear? Let me check: Mute's cannot list is only "Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute CAN hear and CAN see gestures presumably (not listed as cannot). Let me re-check table: Mute can "Read the manual". Cannot: "Speak, or touch the bomb". So Mute can hear speech and can see gestures (not restricted).

So I can hear Deaf's speech and see Blind's gestures (Blind has none available really, but could gesture blanks). I need to encode the mapping via gestures to Deaf, since Deaf will then need to tell Blind the wire color by speech.

I need to wait for Deaf to tell me (via gesture, which I can see) what light is on the bomb. Let me encode colors as gesture symbols for Deaf to use, and establish the mapping now preemptively won't work since Deaf hasn't seen the bomb reported to me yet - actually Deaf sees the bomb directly, no need to report to me. Deaf needs to know which wire to cut. I need to send Deaf the mapping via gesture, then Deaf tells Blind via speech.

I'll assign symbols to colors and send the full mapping to Deaf now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👆]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫱 ✌ 🖐]

I need to reconsider - my gesture scheme from turn 1 was arbitrary and I never actually established what those symbols mean with Deaf beforehand, so Deaf couldn't have understood them either. That was a mistake - sending an undefined code is useless since Deaf has no way to know what 👍🤟 etc. mean without prior agreement.

Now Deaf has sent me gestures back - 4 groups of symbols. Since gestures only carry blanks-vs-symbols information and I can actually see symbols (I'm not blind), I do receive the actual symbols. But I don't know what Deaf intends them to mean either, since we never agreed on an encoding.

I need to restart with a clear, self-explanatory scheme. The key insight: I should not try to encode arbitrary colors - instead I should use gestures that let Deaf identify a color by process of elimination, or better: since Deaf can see the bomb's actual printed colors, I should ask Deaf to describe the light color using colors already visible on the bomb itself — but gestures carry no color meaning inherently.

Better approach: use counting. Assign light colors to gesture counts: 1 symbol = blue light, 2 symbols = green light, 3 symbols = red light. Then Deaf replies with matching count for wire color: 1 = yellow, 2 = green, 3 = blue. This is self-explanatory via structure (count), not arbitrary symbol identity.

Let me send this scheme now, explicitly structured as counts, and ask Deaf to gesture back a count matching the light seen.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👍 ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👍 👍 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎 ☝]

Deaf is sending back structured responses, seemingly echoing my counts and appending a distinct symbol each time - possibly trying to establish their own encoding for the three light colors (blue/green/red) using a fixed prefix count plus a distinguishing symbol. This looks like Deaf is proposing: light=blue → [👍 ☝], light=green → [👍 👍 ✌], light=red → [👍 👍 👍 🤟], and then a separate message [👎 ☝] possibly meaning "this is what I see" or a fourth category.

This is ambiguous and we're burning turns talking past each other. I need to simplify drastically and make my scheme unmistakable by using pure counts with no extra symbols, and explicitly using counts 1/2/3 for the three cut-wire colors directly (skipping the light entirely, since only Deaf needs to know the mapping and only Deaf can see the light - Deaf will map light→wire himself once I give him the manual, then gesture the WIRE color count to me isn't needed either since Deaf can't speak to Blind about... wait Deaf CAN speak).

Key realization: **Deaf can speak**, and **Blind can hear**. So Deaf can directly tell Blind the cut wire color, once Deaf knows the manual mapping! I don't need to relay anything back from Deaf - I just need to teach Deaf the mapping clearly, then Deaf sees the light, looks up the wire color, and speaks it to Blind directly.

My job is done once Deaf understands the mapping. Let me use unambiguous pure counts: count 1 = blue/yellow, count 2 = green/green, count 3 = red/blue, sent as light-count then pause then wire-count, in three separate clearly separated messages, each with two groups.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind. I feel a button embossed push to defeat, and three wires, positions one two three, no other markings. I need instructions on what to do. Please tell me what the manual says.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Progress! Blind spoke and I can hear it - confirms wires are only distinguished by position (1,2,3), no colors Blind can feel. So Blind needs to know which *position* to cut, not a color name - color is useless to Blind since Blind can't see. This means Deaf must be the one who both sees the light AND presumably sees which wire is which color (if wires are visually colored, only Deaf can see that), then Deaf must tell Blind the position number to cut, via speech (which Blind can hear).

Deaf just gestured back [☝] [✌] [🤟] - three single-symbol messages, possibly acknowledging receipt of my three light/wire pairs with a single symbol each (maybe just confirming: "got it, got it, got it" one per pair), or trying to establish their own labels for blue/green/red.

Since Blind can hear Deaf speak, and Deaf can see the bomb (light color and wire colors/positions), the critical remaining link is: Deaf needs to know the manual mapping (light→wire color), then Deaf looks at the bomb to see which position corresponds to that color, and speaks the position number to Blind.

I already sent Deaf the light/wire color pairs via counts (1=blue/yellow, 2=green/green, 3=red/blue). I should confirm this is understood and also tell Blind directly (since I can only gesture to Deaf, not reach Blind - but wait, can I speak to Blind? No, I cannot speak at all). So I must rely on Deaf to relay to Blind via speech.

Let me send one more clarifying gesture set to confirm the mapping direction, using distinct clear structure, then let Deaf act.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👉", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✌]

Deaf has sent only two pairs this time, not three - [👍 🤟] and [✌ ✌]. This matches exactly two of my three mappings: (1→3, i.e., blue→yellow) and (2→2, i.e., green→green). This strongly suggests Deaf is confirming understanding of my scheme by echoing back pairs, but only sending two - possibly because Deaf has identified which one is actually relevant (the light on the bomb) and is confirming just that one, or testing pairs incrementally.

Wait, actually maybe Deaf is telling ME something: perhaps Deaf is using MY symbols to report what the bomb's actual light color is, using my own count-encoding back at me since Deaf now understands my scheme (1=blue, 2=green, 3=red) and legitimately picked one of them corresponding to the bomb's real light, then paired it with the wire color count as confirmation.

[👍 🤟] = light 1 (blue) → wire 3 (which by my color-mapping would be red's wire=blue, count 3). But I intended pair format as (light-count, wire-count) where wire count should equal same index for matching color name... Actually my last message associated: 1→3 meaning blue's wire is yellow(count3)? No — I mapped 1=blue,2=green,3=red for LIGHT, and separately 1=yellow,2=green,3=blue for WIRE. So blue light → yellow wire = light(1) maps to wire(1), not wire(3). I made an indexing error previously by using ✌✌ and 🤟🤟🤟 same-number pairing for green/green and red/blue mismatched.

This is getting tangled. Given the risk, the safest move now is to have Deaf simply describe what they see in plain terms so I can directly tell Blind the wire position - but I can't speak to Blind directly anyway. I must trust Deaf to finish the job now, since further gesture exchange risks more confusion and any wrong action detonates the bomb. I'll send one final unambiguous confirmation and let Deaf proceed with speaking to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👉","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👉","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","👉","🤟"])
```

TURN 6

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👉 👍]

Deaf has now echoed back exactly [👍 👉 👍] - matching my first pair only (light=blue(1) → wire=yellow(1)). This is a strong signal: Deaf is confirming "the light I see is blue, and per your mapping, the wire I need is yellow." Deaf picked out the one relevant pair from the three I sent, meaning the bomb's actual light is blue, and Deaf now knows to cut the yellow wire.

Deaf's job now is to look at the three wires, identify which one is yellow, and speak that position to Blind. I don't need to do anything more here - my mapping was received and Deaf isolated the correct pair. I should not send more noise that could confuse things. I'll wait and let Deaf proceed to instruct Blind directly via speech.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow, light is blue, display shows zero. What does the manual say to do given this? I can cut a wire by position number one two or three, or push the button.

Now I have full clarity. Blind reports what Deaf told them: light is blue, wire one is blue, wire two is green, wire three is yellow. Per the manual: light=blue → cut wire color yellow. Yellow is wire position three.

Blind is asking me to confirm the manual instruction. I cannot speak to Blind directly, but I can gesture to Deaf, who can then speak to Blind. I need to tell Deaf: light blue → cut yellow → that's wire three, so Deaf should tell Blind to cut wire position 3.

I'll gesture to Deaf using a clear, minimal signal: point/count to "3" to indicate the wire position, since Deaf already understands the color mapping and now has the wire-color-to-position info from feeling... wait, Deaf reported the colors themselves, so Deaf already knows wire three = yellow = the one to cut. Deaf just needs to relay "cut wire three" to Blind via speech.

I'll send a confirming gesture to Deaf to reinforce: yes, cut the yellow wire (position 3).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","👍"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 ✊]

I need to use only symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me use a clear count-based gesture to indicate "wire position three" using three taps of the same symbol, which we've already used as a counting convention.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍"])
```
